title: The torsion subsheaf of an injective complex with torsion cohomology is quasi-isomorphic
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention], with abelian sheaf category $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $I^\bullet$ be a cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of injective objects [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$. Call an abelian sheaf $F$ torsion if for every $U\in\mathcal C$ and $s\in F(U)$ there are a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and positive integers $n_i$ with $n_is|_{U_i}=0$. For each degree $r$ let $I^r_{\mathrm{tor}}\subseteq I^r$ be the subsheaf of sections with this property; the differentials preserve these subsheaves, giving a subcomplex $I^\bullet_{\mathrm{tor}}$. If every cohomology sheaf $H^r(I^\bullet)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is torsion, then the inclusion $I^\bullet_{\mathrm{tor}}\hookrightarrow I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No boundedness of $I^\bullet$ and no common annihilator is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, lemma-torsion, proof: divisibility of injectives and the quasi-isomorphism I_tor^bullet -> I^bullet.

proof.text: Write $T^r=I^r_{\mathrm{tor}}$. These are subsheaves: restrictions preserve local annihilation; on a common refinement, if $ns=0$ and $mt=0$ then $nm(s+t)=0$ and $n(-s)=0$; a glued section is locally torsion by composing its gluing cover with the annihilating covers. The covering refinements and composition are those of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Since $d(ns)=n\,d(s)$, every differential carries $T^r$ into $T^{r+1}$. The identities $d^2=0$ restrict, so the inclusions form a morphism of complexes $j:T^\bullet\to I^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, label lemma-torsion, first two proof paragraphs; agent-written local cycle expansion: the torsion subsheaves form a subcomplex.

proof.text: For every degree $q$ and positive integer $n$, [lem-trf-injective-abelian-sheaf-divisible] makes $n:I^q\to I^q$ epic. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], every section $b\in I^q(U)$ therefore has, after a covering of $U$, a section $b'$ with $nb'=b$. This assertion applies to every integer degree, including $r-1$ and $r-2$, and does not choose an annihilator for an entire sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, label lemma-torsion, first two proof paragraphs; agent-written local cycle expansion: divisibility of injective terms, used in the local corrections.

proof.text: For either complex $A^\bullet=I^\bullet$ or $T^\bullet$, put $Z_A^q=\ker d_A^q$ and $B_A^q=\operatorname{im}d_A^{q-1}$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $H^q(A)=Z_A^q/B_A^q$. The quotient $Z_A^q\twoheadrightarrow H^q(A)$ and the image-factorization arrow $A^{q-1}\twoheadrightarrow B_A^q$ are epimorphisms. The local lifting criterion [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] and sectionwise kernels [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] give two precise rules: a cohomology section is locally represented by a genuine cycle $z\in A^q(U)$, and a cycle represents zero exactly when, after a covering, $z=d b$ for a section $b\in A^{q-1}$. For the reverse implication, local vanishing is global vanishing by the sheaf separation axiom. These rules concern sheaf quotients; no quotient of global-section groups is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, label lemma-torsion, first two proof paragraphs; agent-written local cycle expansion: local meaning of cycles, boundaries, and cohomology classes.

proof.text: Fix $r$ and a local section $h$ of $H^r(I)$. Using step 3, first refine to represent it by a cycle $z\in I^r(U)$. The torsion hypothesis gives a further cover and, on each member, a positive integer $n$ with $nh=0$. Step 3 then gives, after another cover, $b\in I^{r-1}(U)$ with $db=nz$. By step 2 choose locally $b'\in I^{r-1}(U)$ with $nb'=b$. The section $z'=z-db'$ satisfies $d z'=0$ and $nz'=nz-db=0$; hence it is a cycle in $T^r$ with image $h$. Covers compose by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Thus every section of $H^r(I)$ locally lifts to $H^r(T)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] makes $H^r(j)$ epic.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, label lemma-torsion, first two proof paragraphs; agent-written local cycle expansion: local surjectivity on cohomology by dividing a primitive.

proof.text: Fix a section $a\in H^r(T)(U)$ with $H^r(j)(a)=0$. Step 3 lets us represent $a$ locally by a cycle $z\in T^r(U)$ and, since its image vanishes, refine until $z=db$ for $b\in I^{r-1}(U)$. Refine once more until a positive integer $n$ kills $z$. Then $d(nb)=nz=0$. The class of $nb$ in $H^{r-1}(I)$ is torsion, so locally there is a positive integer $m$ with $[mnb]=0$; by step 3 refine until $mnb=dc$ for $c\in I^{r-2}(U)$. Step 2, now in degree $r-2$ with the positive integer $mn$, gives locally $c'$ with $mn c'=c$. Set $b'=b-dc'$. Then $mn b'=mnb-dc=0$ and $db'=db=z$, so $b'\in T^{r-1}(U)$ is a torsion primitive of $z$. Consequently $a$ is locally zero in $H^r(T)$, hence zero by sheaf separation. Sectionwise kernels [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] imply that $H^r(j)$ has zero kernel and is monic.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, label lemma-torsion, first two proof paragraphs; agent-written local cycle expansion: local injectivity on cohomology, using torsion also in degree $r-1$.

proof.text: For each $r$, steps 4 and 5 show that every section of $H^r(I)$ has locally a unique preimage in $H^r(T)$. The preimages agree on overlaps by injectivity, and therefore glue by the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Thus $H^r(j)$ is an isomorphism for every integer $r$. This is exactly the definition of a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The argument uses only the finitely many degrees $r,r-1,r-2$ for each $r$ and only integers chosen after local refinements, so it imposes neither a bound on the complex nor a common annihilator.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, label lemma-torsion, first two proof paragraphs; agent-written local cycle expansion: conclusion in every degree, with no boundedness assumption.
